Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: Digital ID portal (did.ecitizen.go.ke) provides facial and fingerprint biometric authentication. Maisha Card has encrypted microprocessor chip for electronic verification with QR code. e-Maisha digital platform enables biometric/PIN/OTP authentication for online transactions. National Public Key Infrastructure (NPKI) supports secure digital identity. eCitizen uses two-factor authentication.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: eCitizen platform (accounts.ecitizen.go.ke) is the unified government portal with 16,000+ services accessible via national ID. 13+ million registered users as of mid-2024. Biometric health identification (BHI) deployed at all Level 4-6 public hospitals. eCitizen generates KES 700 million/day in government collections. Gava Mkononi mobile app extends access.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Data Protection Act 2019 grants data subjects rights to access their data and information about processing. eCitizen platform displays some profile information. However, no right to access processing activity logs exists. Temple iLIT (2025) notes no mechanism for accessing full processing records. Correction mechanism for Maisha Namba is unclear. DPIA was not shared publicly.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: IPRS connected to all financial institutions and telecoms for real-time identity verification. Maisha Namba enables KYC/AML compliance for banks and fintechs. National ID mandatory to open bank accounts, access M-Pesa, obtain credit. Youverify and other providers offer Maisha Namba-based KYC APIs. 84% of adults use mobile money requiring ID-based KYC.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Courts have actively exercised oversight: High Court halted NIIMS in 2020 pending data protection framework; annulled Huduma Card rollout in 2021 requiring DPIA; issued temporary injunctions on Maisha Namba in 2024. Multiple constitutional petitions active (NRF case, Katiba Institute, Haki na Sheria Initiative). However, no accessible administrative review mechanism; only costly constitutional challenges available.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Direct integration between civil registration and digital ID: Maisha Namba assigned at birth registration, serving as the birth certificate number for newborns. Civil Registration Services (CRS) feeds directly into IPRS. Maisha Namba becomes the national ID at age 18 and death certificate number upon death - full lifecycle integration.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Data Protection Act 2019 provides general framework for data sharing. IPRS connected to MDAs, banks, and telecoms for identity verification. However, the data-sharing architecture and rules specific to Maisha Namba are not publicly disclosed. Temple iLIT (2025) notes data sharing framework is not transparent. No comprehensive published data sharing policy for digital ID.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: NIIMS Regulations 2020 and Registration of Persons (Amendment) Regulations 2023 are specific to the digital ID system. However, no standalone comprehensive Digital ID Act has been enacted. The Huduma Bill 2019 was never passed. Maisha Namba relies on secondary legislation under broader registration laws.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Data Protection Act No. 24 of 2019 came into force November 2019. Comprehensive legislation modelled on GDPR. Establishes Office of Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC). Data Protection (General) Regulations 2021 operationalise the Act. Note: national security exception exempts some ID data processing from full DPA coverage.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: Office of Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) established under DPA 2019; Commissioner appointed November 2020. Mandated to oversee compliance, maintain register of data controllers/processors, investigate complaints, conduct inspections. Government conducted 10+ DPIAs for digital ID with ODPC support. However, national security exception limits DPA coverage of Maisha Namba data.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: NIIMS Regulations 2020, Section 9 explicitly states that presentation of the Huduma card or Huduma Namba authenticated by biometrics constitutes sufficient proof of identity. Maisha Card serves as legal ID for government services, passports, and EAC travel. Accepted for banking, SIM registration, and all public services.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Legal basis derives from Registration of Persons Act 1947 (amended 2018), NIIMS Regulations 2020, and Registration of Persons (Amendment) Regulations 2023. Framework relies primarily on secondary legislation rather than a dedicated primary Digital ID Act. Courts found the framework inadequate in 2020 and 2021. Temple iLIT (2025) concluded legal authority is inadequate. Ongoing litigation.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Maisha Namba collects fingerprints (all 10), facial photographs, and iris scans. Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) in use. DNA and GPS data collection was halted by 2020 High Court ruling. Multi-modal biometric collection confirmed.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Centralised NIIMS/IPRS biometric master database stores all personal and biometric data. NRB operates an Electronic Document Management System (EDMS) with 37 million registration records. Hub-and-spoke model connects biometric database to functional databases (KRA, NSSF, NHIF, NEMIS).

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Kenya operates the Maisha Namba/NIIMS system launched in 2023, a third-generation electronic ID (Maisha Card) with biometric chip, UPI assigned at birth, and National Population Master Register. 13+ million enrolled by mid-2024, targeting 32 million adults. System operational but mid-rollout with ongoing legal challenges.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: IPRS connected to all MDAs, financial institutions, and telecoms. PS confirmed NRB, civil registration, and immigration all connected through IPRS interoperability. Maisha Namba linked to NEMIS, SHA/NHIF, KRA, NSSF, eCitizen, land registries. Hub-and-spoke architecture with multiple government databases.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Maisha Namba assigned at birth during civil registration - newborns receive UPI immediately. System is lifecycle-based from birth to death. Traditional national ID issued at age 18. Birth registration linked directly to Maisha Namba assignment, making coverage theoretically universal from birth.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Registration of Persons Act makes ID mandatory for citizens 18+. De facto mandatory: ID required to access banking, SIM cards, NHIF/SHA healthcare, social protection, NEMIS school enrollment, M-Pesa. PS stated registration is 'voluntary' but inability to obtain ID bars access to all major services. No legal penalty for non-enrollment but service exclusion is universal.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: NIIMS Regulations 2020 define 'resident individual' to include citizens and foreign nationals with lawful residency. eCitizen Digital ID terms explicitly include 'Kenyan Citizens, Residents, Refugees, and Foreigners'. 2025 SIM registration regulations recognise Refugee Identity Card. Foreigners/Residents have access to some (not all) government services via eCitizen.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID required for NSSF (national social security), social protection programs for orphans, vulnerable children, sick, and aged. NEMIS school enrollment requires parental ID and child UPI. Maisha Namba is required field for NEMIS enrollment per 2024 civil society interviews. Without digital ID: barred from all social support programs.
